chunks: And it was narrated from Ḥārith, the seller of mats:
that Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who made a bequest for a hajj, so he said:
"If he was a ṣarūrah, then it is from the principal of his wealth; it is only a debt upon him. And if he had already performed hajj, then it is from the one-third."

key_terms.أَوْصَى: made a bequest or testamentary instruction
key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: one-third of the estate available for bequests
key_terms.بِحَجَّةٍ: for a hajj to be performed on his behalf
key_terms.حَارِثٍ: Ḥārith, the narrator mentioned in the report
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: a debt owed and therefore legally due
key_terms.صَرُورَةً: a person who has not yet performed the obligatory hajj
key_terms.صُلْبِ مَالِهِ: the principal or core of his estate

ai.seo_question: When is a deceased person's bequeathed hajj paid from the whole estate rather than one-third?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a bequest for hajj on behalf of the deceased. If the deceased had never performed the obligatory hajj, its cost is taken from the main estate because it is treated as a debt. If he had already performed hajj, then the bequest is fulfilled from one-third of the estate.
